lines.text: I woke up in my own bed, eight days later. They had carried me home across the ice on one of Tobin's sledges.
Ash was on my left. Rook, Birk and Tarn were on my feet. And Bram was asleep in a chair, which I had never once seen in my life.
I wasn't asleep, my lord. I was guarding you. With my eyes shut.
My fingertips were black again. Ilse said they would heal. Probably.
One night. That's all it lasted. At dawn the light went out of them, and every ring settled back where it had been. But for one night, Lucan, you made a village of knights.
The old books have a word for it. A Tide.
And Dunn?
Wren wouldn't let anyone bury him until you woke. She has sat with him every night.
Ilse told me the rest. At Kesting, while I slept, one of the six Measurers came to my sledge with his lens. Brother Aldo. The same man Hask had sent south for the warrant.
The warrant is lawful, Captain. Under the King's own seal. Measure him now, while he can't stop us.
That boy saved two hundred of the King's soldiers. I'll not put chains on him in his sleep. Put the lens away, Brother. Or I'll put it away for you.
He took his column south that same day. To tell the King himself, he said, that his soldiers owed their lives to Greyhollow.
On the ninth day, Halvard Kesting rode into Greyhollow, walked into my hall, and knelt.
I've knelt to two kings and one bear in my life, boy. You're the smallest. And my knees are complaining.
My sons are in that pass. My keep is yours. And so am I, if you'll have an old bear.
I'll have him.
The thread that came was thick, and cold, and stubborn as a mountain. My first lord.
My lord. Penhallow's gone. He left the night the sledges came home, while everyone was at the gate. I only looked away for an hour. I'm so sorry.
Ilse went to her room. When she came back, she was holding an empty box.
My letter. The one I wrote last winter, and never sent. Lord Lucan Varr is hollow-born. I have confirmed it. Signed, Magister Ilse Thorne.
I never burned it. I don't know why. And now Penhallow is riding south with it.
The Order thought Ilse had found nothing. Before the month was out, Vance would know she had found everything.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifty-seven, coming soon.
